answer: An agent economy can stop sybils with identity bonds: before bidding, each agent locks stake, and both votes and fees scale with that deposit. At the summit, an attacker who wants extra votes must fund a fresh bond per fake identity; clones that wander between tasks cannot reuse one deposit, and each new inlet of fake accounts ties up more capital. Caught duplicates lose their stake, so a majority costs as much as the whole honest pool.
